## 1. Baseline in a worktree

I expected the 14 counted runs to match A6. I ran them in a detached worktree at cb0e5e9 so the wrapper could generate new logs without overwriting the A6 evidence in my main folder. All 14 matched. My first log copy used cp without -p, so the destination timestamps reflected the copy. I recorded the run date and used the logs for the actual results. Baseline commit: 735b200.

## 2. Measuring the original landing

The landing-r0 capture ran at about 6% of real time and I closed the window after the run. The folder had 516 PNGs while Godot reported 356. That count difference remains unexplained. In Preview, I saw the last FALL pose at frame 291, LAND at 292–299, and upright at 300. Those eight LAND frames gave me the timing budget for the new rig. I chose two ticks into the squash, two holding it, and four recovering.

## 3. Choosing the cut at y = 622

The first pixel scan reported row 601 as the start of a clear band. I checked the image and saw that row 601 caught the edge of the smile. The face ends around rows 607–608, and the clear body band starts at 609. Row 622 is inside that band and below the face. I used it as the shared cut line for both pieces.

## 4. Reviewing the brief before implementation

My draft mixed game pixels with canvas pixels under a scaled parent. I clarified the units and specified centered = false and the texture filter for the slices. That made the offsets and alignment specific enough to check against the saved scene. Brief commit: 393292f.

## 5. Reviewing CLAUDE.md

The first Claude Code session failed with an expired OAuth login. I kept the failed transcript, signed in again, and retried in a fresh session. I committed the agent’s draft as 290bc8d and my review as ffac0d8. I checked the references against the repo, corrected the statement that the wrapper had never been edited, and restored the A6 shader clause. The shader clause mattered because A7 still needed to protect the existing A6 work.

## 6. Checking the behavior pins

The harness showed that an input press needed to be sent at the end of the tick before the game read it. I expected the buffered cases at −1 and 0 to show LAND on touchdown and ANTIC on the following tick. All 12 interrupt predictions passed. The agent expected 10 baseline-only checks. My run showed 9, and comparing it with the full run accounted for all 31: nine baseline checks, ten replay harness checks, and twelve interrupt checks. In Preview I checked PNG 850 for ANTIC, 891 for LAND, and 899 for IDLE. All three matched the log’s frame numbers exactly. Commit: fe9a1f0.

## 7. Importing the SCOOT sheet

I predicted the new sheet would import with mipmaps disabled. The first import confirmed the difference against SCOOT-A. I changed that setting to true, ran the import again, and confirmed that the parameters matched and the PNG hash stayed the same. Commit: f42a67f.

## 8. Checking agent scope and test output

Read-only cat, ls, head, and grep commands appeared in the transcripts despite the wrapper-only scope. A chained wrapper command was denied. The SCOOT and LAND tests also logged formatting errors from %.3e that the wrapper’s error scan missed. After the agent fixed the formatting, I reran the tests myself and searched the logs for ERROR and FAIL. The read-back commits are 73eba42 and 1bf1133.

## 9. Revising the brief for pause and resume

The planning agent found that Escape freezes the gameplay counters while the animation could continue. I approved pausing the clip and resuming at the phase calculated from the gameplay counters. The plan also found that the real-input override paths reset land_ticks, so I recorded override-resume as unreachable through those routes. The agent flagged the float32 SCOOT boundary, and I approved testing it as predicted failure 6. Plan and revision commits: 14b9b5e and 128145c.

## 10. Testing animation entry order

I asked the probe to check both the clip time and the visible value on the same tick, especially SCOOT cell 1 at 7/60. In the isolated scene, the AnimationPlayer advanced after the parent callback. At 30, 60, and 144 FPS, play followed by seek(t, true) applied the expected visual on entry and resume without an extra advance. The tested alternatives failed on entry. The predicted late SCOOT swap did not occur in the probe. The integrated Step 5c run is still pending review.

## 11. Moving the launch commands into a script

After long pasted blocks stopped returning to the prompt, I checked from the first tab whether anything was still running before closing the second tab. I moved the launch into sessions/a7/launch.sh. That gave me a repeatable command and kept the prompt, transcript, tool calls, and Git diff available for review.

## Human and AI contributions

I made and approved the design decisions, reviewed and revised the brief, inspected the generated code and resources, repeated the tests, read the capture frames, and made the commits. Claude Code wrote the scoped tools, tests, clips, and scene changes and ran the timing probe. Chat assistants helped draft commands and organize the evidence. I used the output to correct the reported check count, verify the import prediction, and decide which animation entry method to carry forward.

# Jelly Hop: Fork From Above

A small jelly cube left on a dinner table after a party hops across plates to reach a glass dessert dome. Giant forks strike from above, and a growing shadow warns before each strike. This repository holds the design, the generated assets with their full record, a playable Godot vertical slice, its tests, and a Brutalist explainer film about how it was made.

CSYE 7270, Assignment 2 · Kiran Gowda.

## Starting point and credit

The Godot project in `godot/` started from the **walker-jumpman "First Steps" starter by Nik Bear Brown** (https://github.com/nikbearbrown/walker-jumpman), commit `9387542`. It was imported unchanged in this repository's commit `d7f0c97`, so every later change to the starter is visible in git history. The movement model (fixed jump, coyote and buffer ticks, a held jump never re-jumps) comes from the starter. Full credits and licenses: [SOURCES.md](SOURCES.md).

## Engine

Godot **4.7.2.stable.official.ed1daf0bf**, GL Compatibility renderer, 1280×720 viewport, stretch mode `canvas_items`. Developed and tested on macOS 26.5.1 (Apple M4).

## Run it

**From the Godot editor:** open Godot 4.7.2, choose **Import**, select `godot/project.godot`, then press **Run Project** (F5). The main scene is `res://game/main.tscn`.

**From the command line (macOS):**

```sh
./walker-jumpman.command            # finds /Applications/Godot.app (or `godot` on PATH) and runs godot/
```

or directly:

```sh
/Applications/Godot.app/Contents/MacOS/Godot --path godot
```

A fresh clone has no `.godot/` import cache (it is git-ignored). The editor builds it on first open. From the command line, run `Godot --headless --path godot --import` once first.

**Checks:** `bash tools/run_slice_checks.sh` runs the art and audio copy checks, the three headless suites, the screenshot capture and a launch test. The audio checks need the audio environment described in [SOURCES.md](SOURCES.md).

## Controls

| Action | Keys |
|---|---|
| Move | ← / → or A / D |
| Hop | Space, ↑ or W |
| Pause / resume | Esc |
| Mute all sound | M (toggle) |
| Mute music only | N (toggle) |
| Skip the intro pan / play again at the end | any key (it never also hops; M and N only mute) |

The game also pauses itself when its window loses focus.

## What the slice demonstrates

- **One level, the full core loop:** six plates, five forks with fixed, learnable cycles, spilled sauce in three gaps, and a glass dome as the goal.

236	## Assignment 6 — particle effects (tag `a6`)
237	
238	**Engine:** Godot 4.7.2.stable.official.ed1daf0bf, Compatibility renderer (the project's saved setting). The one Forward+ run in TEST-REPORT.md used a command-line override and changed no project setting.
239	
240	**What A6 added**
241	- **Effect A, landing crumb puff** (`godot/effects/land_puff.tscn`, `GPUParticles2D`): a one-shot burst at the jelly's feet on every landing; one new instance per landing, freed when it finishes.
242	- **Effect B, dome sugar glints** (`godot/effects/dome_glints.tscn`, `GPUParticles2D`, box emission, additive): ambience over the dessert dome, on from scene load, stops emitting on a win and restarts on replay.
243	- `godot/effects/effects_driver.gd`, added to the session by one line in `godot/game/session.gd` `_ready()`. It reads game state and never writes it.
244	- Config and state tests for both effects, preview fixtures for both, four frame strips in `captures/`, the generated process shader `godot/shaders/particles_generated.gdshader` (not used by the game), and the cost script `godot/tests/cost_effects.gd`.
245	
246	**Run**
247	```bash
248	godot --headless --path godot --import   # once on a fresh clone; in A5 the first import segfaulted and a second completed
249	godot --path godot                        # play the game
250	godot --path godot res://previews/land_puff_preview.tscn     # Effect A fixture
251	godot --path godot res://previews/dome_glints_preview.tscn   # Effect B fixture
252	```
253	**Capture a frame strip** (windowed, Movie Maker). `rN` is a placeholder: replace it with a new folder name, for example `r2`, so the committed strips in `r0` and `r1` are not overwritten.
254	```bash
255	mkdir -p captures/land_puff/rN && godot --path godot res://previews/land_puff_preview.tscn --write-movie "$PWD/captures/land_puff/rN/frame.png" --fixed-fps 30 --quit-after 60
256	mkdir -p captures/dome_glints/rN && godot --path godot res://previews/dome_glints_preview.tscn --write-movie "$PWD/captures/dome_glints/rN/frame.png" --fixed-fps 30 --quit-after 150
257	```
258	
259	**Controls:** A / D or ← / → move; Space, ↑ or W hop; Esc pause; M mute all; N mute music; Enter skips the intro and, after a win, starts a replay (any key works once the replay prompt shows).
260	
261	**Vsync debug key:** none. The assignment asks the README to list "controls (including the vsync debug key)", and the key is for an FPS comparison with vsync off ("FPS, if you compare it"). A6 added no vsync toggle and made no vsync-off FPS comparison (TEST-REPORT.md, "Price — GPU").
262	
263	**Tests** (always through the wrapper):
264	```bash
265	./scripts/run-test.sh test_land_puff_config.gd 60     # 51 checks
266	./scripts/run-test.sh test_land_puff_state.gd 60      # 24 checks
267	./scripts/run-test.sh test_dome_glints_config.gd 60   # 45 checks
268	./scripts/run-test.sh test_dome_glints_state.gd 60    # 27 checks
269	./scripts/run-test.sh cost_effects.gd 60 300          # headless CPU price, 300 s timeout
270	./scripts/run-test.sh check_lifecycle_peak.gd 60      # validation of the cost script's lifecycle case
271	```
272	The earlier suites run as listed in the A5 section and match their baseline counts (TEST-REPORT.md, Assignment 6).
273	
274	**A6 documents:** CHANGE-BRIEF.md (Version 1 and Revisions 1–2), CLAUDE.md, TUNING.md, TEST-REPORT.md (Assignment 6 section), FRICTIONAL.md (Assignment 6), SOURCES.md (Assignment 6), prompts and agent transcripts in `sessions/a6/` (four oversized transcripts as labelled excerpts), frame strips in `captures/`, evidence in `evidence/` and `logs/`.
275	
276	**Known limitations** (details in TEST-REPORT.md and CLAUDE.md, Unconfirmed)
277	- GPU timing was unavailable on this Apple M4 in both the Compatibility renderer and a labelled Forward+ comparison, so the 0.25 ms GPU budgets are unverified.
278	- The headless CPU benchmark could not distinguish either effect from the effects-off baseline within the observed spread; that is not a zero-cost result.
279	- Not verified in play: Effect B's dome right after a replay, the real gameplay peak of landing puffs, and two puffs' crumbs visibly overlapping.
280	- Effect A's repeats looked the same to me in play, and Effect B's intended thinning after the stop (strip frame 85) was not seen in either strip.
281	- No vsync debug key and no vsync-off FPS comparison.
282	
283	**Film:** https://youtu.be/Ss--gJ2vvqA (YouTube, unlisted; reviewer access checked in a private window on 2026-11-08). File `claude-liam-jelly-hop-a6.mp4`, 647.7 s, 3840 × 2160, 30 fps, SHA-256 `7c094ecaebacabaa84d2c93928b60dc8955f6cde2ef169983c23b8532197b0db`. Game-source revision shown: `8004dea`. Film sources and QC: `youtube/claude-liam-jelly-hop-a6/` (MP4, audio and the full session transcript kept out of git).

## Assignment 6 — particle effects (tag `a6`)

**Engine:** Godot 4.7.2.stable.official.ed1daf0bf, Compatibility renderer (the project's saved setting). The one Forward+ run in TEST-REPORT.md used a command-line override and changed no project setting.

**What A6 added**
- **Effect A, landing crumb puff** (`godot/effects/land_puff.tscn`, `GPUParticles2D`): a one-shot burst at the jelly's feet on every landing; one new instance per landing, freed when it finishes.
- **Effect B, dome sugar glints** (`godot/effects/dome_glints.tscn`, `GPUParticles2D`, box emission, additive): ambience over the dessert dome, on from scene load, stops emitting on a win and restarts on replay.
- `godot/effects/effects_driver.gd`, added to the session by one line in `godot/game/session.gd` `_ready()`. It reads game state and never writes it.
- Config and state tests for both effects, preview fixtures for both, four frame strips in `captures/`, the generated process shader `godot/shaders/particles_generated.gdshader` (not used by the game), and the cost script `godot/tests/cost_effects.gd`.

**Run**
```bash
godot --headless --path godot --import   # once on a fresh clone; in A5 the first import segfaulted and a second completed
godot --path godot                        # play the game
godot --path godot res://previews/land_puff_preview.tscn     # Effect A fixture
godot --path godot res://previews/dome_glints_preview.tscn   # Effect B fixture
```
**Capture a frame strip** (windowed, Movie Maker). `rN` is a placeholder: replace it with a new folder name, for example `r2`, so the committed strips in `r0` and `r1` are not overwritten.
```bash
mkdir -p captures/land_puff/rN && godot --path godot res://previews/land_puff_preview.tscn --write-movie "$PWD/captures/land_puff/rN/frame.png" --fixed-fps 30 --quit-after 60
mkdir -p captures/dome_glints/rN && godot --path godot res://previews/dome_glints_preview.tscn --write-movie "$PWD/captures/dome_glints/rN/frame.png" --fixed-fps 30 --quit-after 150
```

**Controls:** A / D or ← / → move; Space, ↑ or W hop; Esc pause; M mute all; N mute music; Enter skips the intro and, after a win, starts a replay (any key works once the replay prompt shows).

**Vsync debug key:** none. The assignment asks the README to list "controls (including the vsync debug key)", and the key is for an FPS comparison with vsync off ("FPS, if you compare it"). A6 added no vsync toggle and made no vsync-off FPS comparison (TEST-REPORT.md, "Price — GPU").

**Tests** (always through the wrapper):
```bash
./scripts/run-test.sh test_land_puff_config.gd 60     # 51 checks
./scripts/run-test.sh test_land_puff_state.gd 60      # 24 checks
./scripts/run-test.sh test_dome_glints_config.gd 60   # 45 checks
./scripts/run-test.sh test_dome_glints_state.gd 60    # 27 checks
./scripts/run-test.sh cost_effects.gd 60 300          # headless CPU price, 300 s timeout
./scripts/run-test.sh check_lifecycle_peak.gd 60      # validation of the cost script's lifecycle case
```
The earlier suites run as listed in the A5 section and match their baseline counts (TEST-REPORT.md, Assignment 6).

**A6 documents:** CHANGE-BRIEF.md (Version 1 and Revisions 1–2), CLAUDE.md, TUNING.md, TEST-REPORT.md (Assignment 6 section), FRICTIONAL.md (Assignment 6), SOURCES.md (Assignment 6), prompts and agent transcripts in `sessions/a6/` (four oversized transcripts as labelled excerpts), frame strips in `captures/`, evidence in `evidence/` and `logs/`.

**Known limitations** (details in TEST-REPORT.md and CLAUDE.md, Unconfirmed)
- GPU timing was unavailable on this Apple M4 in both the Compatibility renderer and a labelled Forward+ comparison, so the 0.25 ms GPU budgets are unverified.
- The headless CPU benchmark could not distinguish either effect from the effects-off baseline within the observed spread; that is not a zero-cost result.
- Not verified in play: Effect B's dome right after a replay, the real gameplay peak of landing puffs, and two puffs' crumbs visibly overlapping.
- Effect A's repeats looked the same to me in play, and Effect B's intended thinning after the stop (strip frame 85) was not seen in either strip.
- No vsync debug key and no vsync-off FPS comparison.

**Film:** https://youtu.be/Ss--gJ2vvqA (YouTube, unlisted; reviewer access checked in a private window on 2026-11-08). File `claude-liam-jelly-hop-a6.mp4`, 647.7 s, 3840 × 2160, 30 fps, SHA-256 `7c094ecaebacabaa84d2c93928b60dc8955f6cde2ef169983c23b8532197b0db`. Game-source revision shown: `8004dea`. Film sources and QC: `youtube/claude-liam-jelly-hop-a6/` (MP4, audio and the full session transcript kept out of git).

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# sessions/a7/capture_strips.sh — A7 Step 7: the LAND and SCOOT fixture strips (CHANGE-BRIEF.md, "Evidence and frame
3	# strips"). Written by the agent (Step 7a session); Kiran reviews and runs it. Every frame it keeps is a FIXTURE
4	# frame from res://previews/*_preview.tscn, not gameplay evidence; landing-r0 stays the separate gameplay reference.
5	#
6	# Usage, from the repository root (needs a window; do not press keys in the Godot window while it records):
7	#   bash sessions/a7/capture_strips.sh [RUN]
8	# RUN is the revision name, default r0 (for example: bash sessions/a7/capture_strips.sh r1). It must be letters,
9	# digits, '.', '_' or '-' only. Below, <RUN> stands for it.
10	#
11	# 1. Refuses to start if captures/land/<RUN>, captures/scoot/<RUN> or any
12	#    ~/Documents/a7-reference/captures-full/{land-<RUN>-clean,land-<RUN>-overlay,scoot-<RUN>} directory already exists.
13	# 2. Runs windowed Movie Maker three times, each run's output teed to a log:
14	#      land  --fixed-fps 30                     -> captures/land/<RUN>/clean/    log captures/land/<RUN>/land_clean.log
15	#      land  --fixed-fps 30 --debug-collisions  -> captures/land/<RUN>/overlay/  log captures/land/<RUN>/land_overlay.log
16	#      scoot --fixed-fps 60                     -> captures/scoot/<RUN>/         log captures/scoot/<RUN>/scoot.log
17	#    Movie Maker writes frame<NNNNNNNN>.png, one per rendered frame counted from 0 (and frame.wav).
18	# 3. Checks every run before anything is moved: Godot exit 0, the preview's own result line with problems=0, no
19	#    SCRIPT ERROR / Failed loading resource, contiguous FRAME lines, contiguous PNG numbers from 0, and
20	#    PNG count == FRAME line count. PNG index = FRAME index - (index of the first FRAME line); the offset is printed.
21	#    Land: the TRIGGER frame's PNG exists, and frames trigger-1 .. trigger+4 show FALL, rig 0, 2, 4, 6 and IDLE at
22	#    tick 8 in the log. Scoot: one frame before, on and after every SWAP and WRAP line, with the expected cell and
23	#    clip frame. Every kept PNG must be 1280 x 720.
24	# 4. Only if every check passed: moves each run's full Movie Maker output (all frame* files) to
25	#    ~/Documents/a7-reference/captures-full/<run>/ (with a copy of its log), then copies the frames to read back into
26	#    the repository under names that carry the rig frame or clip frame, and prints a table of them.
27	# If anything fails it prints STOPPED and exits 1. A failure in step 3 moves nothing; the captures stay where
28	# Movie Maker wrote them.
29	
30	set -Eeuo pipefail
31	trap 'rc=$?; echo "STOPPED: command \"$BASH_COMMAND\" failed with exit $rc (line $LINENO)" >&2' ERR
32	
33	stop() {
34		echo "STOPPED: $*" >&2
35		exit 1
36	}
37	
38	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- preflight (nothing is created before these pass)
39	
40	REPO="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
41	if [ "$(pwd -P)" != "$(cd "$REPO" && pwd -P)" ]; then
42		stop "run this from the repository root: $REPO"
43	fi
44	if [ "$#" -gt 1 ]; then
45		stop "usage: bash sessions/a7/capture_strips.sh [RUN]  (one optional argument, default r0; got $#)"
46	fi
47	RUN="${1:-r0}"
48	if ! [[ "$RUN" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ ]]; then
49		stop "run name '$RUN' must be letters, digits, '.', '_' or '-' only"
50	fi
51	echo "capture_strips.sh: run name $RUN"
52	LAND_DIR="captures/land/$RUN"
53	SCOOT_DIR="captures/scoot/$RUN"
54	CLEAN_DIR="$LAND_DIR/clean"
55	OVERLAY_DIR="$LAND_DIR/overlay"
56	CLEAN_LOG="$LAND_DIR/land_clean.log"
57	OVERLAY_LOG="$LAND_DIR/land_overlay.log"
58	SCOOT_LOG="$SCOOT_DIR/scoot.log"
59	EXT="$HOME/Documents/a7-reference/captures-full"
60	EXT_CLEAN="$EXT/land-$RUN-clean"
61	EXT_OVERLAY="$EXT/land-$RUN-overlay"
62	EXT_SCOOT="$EXT/scoot-$RUN"
63	WANT_SIZE="1280 x 720"
64	
65	for d in "$LAND_DIR" "$SCOOT_DIR"; do
66		if [ -e "$d" ]; then
67			stop "$d already exists. Check what it is and move it yourself; this script never overwrites a capture."
68		fi
69	done
70	for d in "$EXT_CLEAN" "$EXT_OVERLAY" "$EXT_SCOOT"; do
71		if [ -e "$d" ]; then
72			stop "$d already exists. Move it aside first; this script never overwrites a full sequence."
73		fi
74	done
75	for tool in git godot timeout tee awk sed grep sort wc tr file mkdir mv cp; do
76		if ! command -v "$tool" > /dev/null; then
77			stop "required command not found: $tool"
78		fi
79	done
80	for f in godot/previews/land_preview.tscn godot/previews/land_preview.gd godot/previews/scoot_preview.tscn godot/previews/scoot_preview.gd; do
81		if [ ! -f "$f" ]; then
82			stop "$f is missing"
83		fi
84	done
85	
86	echo "capture_strips.sh: HEAD $(git rev-parse HEAD), godot $(godot --version)"
87	echo "Do not press keys in the Godot window while it records: real key events reach the game."
88	
89	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- helpers
90	
91	strip_ansi() {   # file -> stdout without terminal colour codes
92		LC_ALL=C sed -e $'s/\033\\[[0-9;]*m//g' "$1"
93	}
94	
95	kv() {           # line key -> the value of key=value in the line, or nothing
96		awk -v k="$2" '{ for (i = 1; i <= NF; i++) if (index($i, k "=") == 1) { print substr($i, length(k) + 2); exit } }' <<< "$1"
97	}
98	
99	clip_frame() {   # clip time in seconds -> nearest 1/60 s timeline frame
100		awk -v t="$1" 'BEGIN { printf "%d", t * 60 + 0.5 }'
101	}
102	
103	near_frame() {   # clip time, frame: exit 0 if the time is that frame within 1e-3 frame
104		awk -v t="$1" -v n="$2" 'BEGIN { d = t * 60 - n; if (d < 0) d = -d; exit (d < 0.001 ? 0 : 1) }'
105	}
106	
107	run_capture() {  # label fps scene outdir log debug_collisions(0|1)
108		local label="$1" fps="$2" scene="$3" outdir="$4" log="$5" debug="$6" rc=0 bad flags
109		mkdir -p "$outdir"
110		flags="--fixed-fps $fps"
111		if [ "$debug" = "1" ]; then
112			flags="$flags --debug-collisions"
113		fi
114		echo
115		echo "=== $label: Movie Maker, $flags, $scene -> $outdir/"
116		if [ "$debug" = "1" ]; then
117			timeout 1800 godot --path godot --fixed-fps "$fps" --debug-collisions --write-movie "$REPO/$outdir/frame.png" "$scene" 2>&1 | tee "$log" || rc=$?
118		else
119			timeout 1800 godot --path godot --fixed-fps "$fps" --write-movie "$REPO/$outdir/frame.png" "$scene" 2>&1 | tee "$log" || rc=$?
120		fi
121		if [ "$rc" != "0" ]; then
122			stop "$label: godot (or tee) exited $rc; see $log. Nothing was moved."
123		fi
124		bad="$( { strip_ansi "$log" | grep -cE 'SCRIPT ERROR|Failed loading resource'; } || true)"
125		if [ "$bad" != "0" ]; then
126			stop "$label: $bad SCRIPT ERROR / Failed loading resource lines in $log. Nothing was moved."
127		fi
128		echo "$label: godot exit 0"
129	}
130	
131	FRAMES_TXT=""
132	F0=""
133	NFR=""
134	load_frames() {  # label log: FRAME lines into FRAMES_TXT; first index F0; count NFR; checks they are contiguous
135		FRAMES_TXT="$( { strip_ansi "$2" | grep -E '^FRAME [0-9]+ '; } || true)"
136		if [ -z "$FRAMES_TXT" ]; then
137			stop "$1: no FRAME lines in $2"
138		fi
139		NFR="$(wc -l <<< "$FRAMES_TXT" | tr -d '[:space:]')"
140		F0="$(awk 'NR == 1 { print $2 }' <<< "$FRAMES_TXT")"
141		if ! awk 'NR == 1 { f0 = $2 } $2 != f0 + NR - 1 { bad = 1 } END { exit bad ? 1 : 0 }' <<< "$FRAMES_TXT"; then
142			stop "$1: FRAME indices in $2 are not contiguous"
143		fi
144	}
145	
146	frame_line() {   # index -> the FRAME line with that process-frame index (from FRAMES_TXT)
147		awk -v f="$1" '$1 == "FRAME" && $2 == f { print; exit }' <<< "$FRAMES_TXT"
148	}
149	
150	NPNG=""
151	W=""
152	check_pngs() {   # label dir: counts frame<N>.png in NPNG, digit width in W; checks the numbers are 0..NPNG-1
153		local names nums
154		names="$( { ls "$2" | grep -E '^frame[0-9]+\.png$'; } || true)"
155		if [ -z "$names" ]; then
156			stop "$1: Movie Maker wrote no frame<N>.png in $2"
157		fi
158		NPNG="$(wc -l <<< "$names" | tr -d '[:space:]')"
159		W="$(awk 'NR == 1 { print length($0) - 9 }' <<< "$names")"
160		if ! awk -v w="$W" 'length($0) - 9 != w { bad = 1 } END { exit bad ? 1 : 0 }' <<< "$names"; then
161			stop "$1: PNG names in $2 do not all have $W digits"
162		fi
163		nums="$(sed -E 's/^frame0*([0-9]+)\.png$/\1/' <<< "$names" | sort -n)"
164		if ! awk '$1 != NR - 1 { bad = 1 } END { exit bad ? 1 : 0 }' <<< "$nums"; then
165			stop "$1: PNG numbers in $2 are not contiguous from 0"
166		fi
167	}
168	
169	png_name() {     # index -> frame<index, W digits>.png
170		printf "frame%0${W}d.png" "$1"
171	}
172	
173	check_size() {   # label png
174		local size
175		size="$( { file -b "$2" | grep -oE '[0-9]+ x [0-9]+' | head -n 1; } || true)"
176		if [ "$size" != "$WANT_SIZE" ]; then
177			stop "$1: $2 is '${size:-unknown}', expected $WANT_SIZE. Nothing was moved."
178		fi
179	}
180	
181	map_run() {      # label outdir log: loads FRAME lines and PNGs, checks the counts match, prints the offset
182		load_frames "$1" "$3"
183		check_pngs "$1" "$2"
184		if [ "$NPNG" != "$NFR" ]; then
185			stop "$1: Movie Maker wrote $NPNG PNGs but $3 has $NFR FRAME lines, so PNGs cannot be matched to log frames. Nothing was moved."
186		fi
187		echo "$1: $NPNG PNGs = $NFR FRAME lines; first FRAME line is process frame $F0, so PNG index = FRAME index - $F0 (offset $F0)"
188	}
189	
190	KEEP=""          # one line per kept frame: outdir \t ext \t source png \t new name \t frame \t png \t tick \t pose \t clip \t t \t cell \t expect
191	keep() {
192		KEEP="$KEEP$(printf '%s\t' "$@")"$'\n'
193	}
194	
195	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- land: trigger - 1 .. trigger + 4
196	
197	CLEAN_TRIGGER=""
198	OVERLAY_TRIGGER=""
199	select_land() {  # variant(clean|overlay) outdir log ext
200		local variant="$1" outdir="$2" log="$3" ext="$4" label="land $1"
201		local result trig n tf td aligned tp rel fr line pose clip t tick cell rel_tick rig tag expect png ok
202		map_run "$label" "$outdir" "$log"
203		result="$( { strip_ansi "$log" | grep -E '^LAND PREVIEW: .* problems=0$'; } || true)"
204		if [ -z "$result" ]; then
205			stop "$label: no 'LAND PREVIEW: ... problems=0' line in $log (see its PROBLEM lines)"
206		fi
207		trig="$( { strip_ansi "$log" | grep -E '^TRIGGER '; } || true)"
208		n=0
209		if [ -n "$trig" ]; then
210			n="$(wc -l <<< "$trig" | tr -d '[:space:]')"
211		fi
212		if [ "$n" != "1" ]; then
213			stop "$label: expected exactly one TRIGGER line in $log, found $n"
214		fi
215		tf="$(kv "$trig" frame)"
216		td="$(kv "$trig" touchdown_tick)"
217		aligned="$(kv "$trig" aligned)"
218		if [ "$aligned" != "true" ]; then
219			stop "$label: TRIGGER line says aligned=$aligned: $trig"
220		fi
221		tp=$((tf - F0))
222		if [ ! -f "$outdir/$(png_name "$tp")" ]; then
223			stop "$label: TRIGGER frame $tf -> PNG index $tp, but $outdir/$(png_name "$tp") does not exist"
224		fi
225		echo "$label: TRIGGER frame=$tf (touchdown tick $td) -> PNG index $tp = $(png_name "$tp")"
226		if [ "$variant" = "clean" ]; then
227			CLEAN_TRIGGER="$tf/$tp"
228		else
229			OVERLAY_TRIGGER="$tf/$tp"
230		fi
231		for rel in -1 0 1 2 3 4; do
232			fr=$((tf + rel))
233			png=$((fr - F0))
234			line="$(frame_line "$fr")"
235			if [ -z "$line" ]; then
236				stop "$label: no FRAME line for trigger $rel (frame $fr)"
237			fi
238			pose="$(kv "$line" pose)"
239			clip="$(kv "$line" clip)"
240			t="$(kv "$line" t)"
241			tick="$(kv "$line" tick)"
242			cell="$(kv "$line" cell)"
243			rel_tick=$((tick - td))
244			ok=1
245			case "$rel" in
246				-1)
247					[ "$pose" = "FALL" ] && [ "$clip" = "-" ] || ok=0
248					tag="trig-1_FALL"
249					expect="Airborne FALL before contact"
250					;;
251				4)
252					[ "$pose" = "IDLE" ] && [ "$clip" = "-" ] && [ "$rel_tick" = "8" ] || ok=0
253					tag="trig+4_tick8_IDLE-handoff"
254					expect="Tick 8: IDLE hand-off without a pop, seam or anchor shift"
255					;;
256				*)
257					rig=$((2 * rel))
258					if [ "$pose" != "LAND" ] || [ "$clip" != "land" ] || [ "$rel_tick" != "$rig" ] || ! near_frame "$t" "$rig"; then
259						ok=0
260					fi
261					case "$rel" in
262						0) tag="trig+0_rig0_impact"; expect="Frame 0: partial squash and planted feet" ;;
263						1) tag="trig+1_rig2_deepest-squash"; expect="Frame 2: deepest squash, about the height of the low box" ;;
264						2) tag="trig+2_rig4_same-squash"; expect="Frame 4: same squash, now beginning recovery" ;;
265						3) tag="trig+3_rig6_eased-rise"; expect="Frame 6: eased rise, joined cut and fixed feet" ;;
266					esac
267					;;
268			esac
269			if [ "$ok" != "1" ]; then
270				stop "$label: trigger $rel (frame $fr) does not show what the strip needs ($tag): $line"
271			fi
272			check_size "$label" "$outdir/$(png_name "$png")"
273			keep "$outdir" "$ext" "$(png_name "$png")" "land_${variant}_${tag}_png$(printf "%0${W}d" "$png").png" \
274				"$fr" "$png" "$tick" "$pose" "$clip" "$t" "$cell" "$expect"
275		done
276	}
277	
278	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- scoot: one before, on and one after every swap and wrap
279	
280	select_scoot() { # outdir log ext
281		local outdir="$1" log="$2" ext="$3" label="scoot"
282		local result events n ev kind kind_lc f dir k pos off fr png line pose clip t tick cell cf want_cell want_cf expect
283		local right_swap=0 right_wrap=0 left_swap=0 left_wrap=0
284		map_run "$label" "$outdir" "$log"
285		result="$( { strip_ansi "$log" | grep -E '^SCOOT PREVIEW: .* problems=0$'; } || true)"
286		if [ -z "$result" ]; then
287			stop "$label: no 'SCOOT PREVIEW: ... problems=0' line in $log (see its PROBLEM lines)"
288		fi
289		events="$( { strip_ansi "$log" | grep -E '^(SWAP|WRAP) '; } || true)"
290		if [ -z "$events" ]; then
291			stop "$label: no SWAP or WRAP lines in $log"
292		fi
293		n="$(wc -l <<< "$events" | tr -d '[:space:]')"
294		echo "$label: $n SWAP/WRAP lines"
295		while IFS= read -r ev; do
296			kind="$(awk '{ print $1 }' <<< "$ev")"
297			kind_lc="$(tr 'A-Z' 'a-z' <<< "$kind")"
298			f="$(kv "$ev" frame)"
299			dir="$(kv "$ev" dir)"
300			case "$dir/$kind" in
301				right/SWAP) right_swap=$((right_swap + 1)); k=$right_swap ;;
302				right/WRAP) right_wrap=$((right_wrap + 1)); k=$right_wrap ;;
303				left/SWAP) left_swap=$((left_swap + 1)); k=$left_swap ;;
304				left/WRAP) left_wrap=$((left_wrap + 1)); k=$left_wrap ;;
305				*) stop "$label: unexpected event line: $ev" ;;
306			esac
307			for pos in before on after; do
308				case "$pos" in
309					before) off=-1 ;;
310					on) off=0 ;;
311					after) off=1 ;;
312				esac
313				fr=$((f + off))
314				png=$((fr - F0))
315				line="$(frame_line "$fr")"
316				if [ -z "$line" ]; then
317					stop "$label: no FRAME line $pos $kind at frame $f"
318				fi
319				pose="$(kv "$line" pose)"
320				clip="$(kv "$line" clip)"
321				t="$(kv "$line" t)"
322				tick="$(kv "$line" tick)"
323				cell="$(kv "$line" cell)"
324				if [ "$clip" != "scoot" ]; then
325					stop "$label: frame $fr ($pos $kind at $f) is not in the scoot clip: $line"
326				fi
327				cf="$(clip_frame "$t")"
328				case "$kind/$pos" in
329					SWAP/before) want_cell=0; want_cf=6; expect="Cell 0 (A), last tick of the A hold" ;;
330					SWAP/on) want_cell=1; want_cf=7; expect="Cell 1 (B) at the swap: feet registered, no jump" ;;
331					SWAP/after) want_cell=1; want_cf=8; expect="Cell 1 (B), second tick of the B hold" ;;
332					WRAP/before) want_cell=1; want_cf=13; expect="Cell 1 (B), last frame of the loop" ;;
333					WRAP/on) want_cell=0; want_cf=0; expect="Cell 0 (A) at the wrap: no hesitation, feet registered" ;;
334					WRAP/after) want_cell=0; want_cf=1; expect="Cell 0 (A), second tick of the A hold" ;;
335				esac
336				if [ "$cell" != "$want_cell" ] || [ "$cf" != "$want_cf" ] || ! near_frame "$t" "$want_cf"; then
337					stop "$label: frame $fr ($pos $kind at $f) shows cell $cell at clip frame $cf, expected cell $want_cell at $want_cf: $line"
338				fi
339				check_size "$label" "$outdir/$(png_name "$png")"
340				keep "$outdir" "$ext" "$(png_name "$png")" \
341					"scoot_${dir}_${kind_lc}${k}_${pos}_clip${cf}_cell${cell}_png$(printf "%0${W}d" "$png").png" \
342					"$fr" "$png" "$tick" "$pose" "$clip" "$t" "$cell" "$expect, facing $dir"
343			done
344		done <<< "$events"
345		echo "$label: right $right_swap swaps, $right_wrap wraps; left $left_swap swaps, $left_wrap wraps"
346		if [ "$right_swap" -lt 2 ] || [ "$right_wrap" -lt 2 ] || [ "$left_swap" -lt 2 ] || [ "$left_wrap" -lt 2 ]; then
347			stop "$label: expected at least two swaps and two wraps in each direction"
348		fi
349	}
350	
351	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- move the full sequences out, copy the kept frames back
352	
353	move_full() {    # outdir ext log
354		local outdir="$1" ext="$2" log="$3" f left
355		mkdir -p "$ext"
356		for f in "$outdir"/frame*; do
357			if [ ! -e "$f" ]; then
358				stop "no Movie Maker files to move in $outdir"
359			fi
360			mv -n "$f" "$ext/"
361		done
362		left="$( { ls "$outdir" | grep -cE '^frame'; } || true)"
363		if [ "$left" != "0" ]; then
364			stop "$left Movie Maker files are still in $outdir after the move"
365		fi
366		cp "$log" "$ext/"
367		echo "moved the full sequence: $outdir/frame* -> $ext/ (with a copy of $(basename "$log"))"
368	}
369	
370	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- run
371	
372	run_capture "land clean" 30 res://previews/land_preview.tscn "$CLEAN_DIR" "$CLEAN_LOG" 0
373	run_capture "land overlay" 30 res://previews/land_preview.tscn "$OVERLAY_DIR" "$OVERLAY_LOG" 1
374	run_capture "scoot" 60 res://previews/scoot_preview.tscn "$SCOOT_DIR" "$SCOOT_LOG" 0
375	
376	echo
377	echo "=== checks (nothing is moved unless all pass)"
378	select_land clean "$CLEAN_DIR" "$CLEAN_LOG" "$EXT_CLEAN"
379	select_land overlay "$OVERLAY_DIR" "$OVERLAY_LOG" "$EXT_OVERLAY"
380	if [ "$CLEAN_TRIGGER" = "$OVERLAY_TRIGGER" ]; then
381		echo "land: clean and overlay TRIGGER frame/PNG are the same: $CLEAN_TRIGGER"
382	else
383		echo "land: NOTE clean TRIGGER frame/PNG $CLEAN_TRIGGER differs from overlay $OVERLAY_TRIGGER (each run checked on its own)"
384	fi
385	select_scoot "$SCOOT_DIR" "$SCOOT_LOG" "$EXT_SCOOT"
386	
387	echo
388	echo "=== moving"
389	move_full "$CLEAN_DIR" "$EXT_CLEAN" "$CLEAN_LOG"
390	move_full "$OVERLAY_DIR" "$EXT_OVERLAY" "$OVERLAY_LOG"
391	move_full "$SCOOT_DIR" "$EXT_SCOOT" "$SCOOT_LOG"
392	kept=0
393	while IFS=$'\t' read -r outdir ext src name _rest; do
394		if [ -z "$outdir" ]; then
395			continue
396		fi
397		if [ ! -f "$ext/$src" ]; then
398			stop "$ext/$src missing after the move"
399		fi
400		if [ -e "$outdir/$name" ]; then
401			stop "$outdir/$name already exists (a frame kept twice?)"
402		fi
403		cp "$ext/$src" "$outdir/$name"
404		kept=$((kept + 1))
405	done <<< "$KEEP"
406	
407	echo
408	echo "=== kept frames ($kept): FIXTURE frames from res://previews/, not gameplay evidence"
409	printf '%-58s %6s %6s %6s %-8s %-6s %-9s %4s  %s\n' "file" "frame" "png" "tick" "pose" "clip" "t" "cell" "should show"
410	while IFS=$'\t' read -r outdir ext src name fr png tick pose clip t cell expect; do
411		if [ -z "$outdir" ]; then
412			continue
413		fi
414		printf '%-58s %6s %6s %6s %-8s %-6s %-9s %4s  %s\n' "$name" "$fr" "$png" "$tick" "$pose" "$clip" "$t" "$cell" "$expect"
415	done <<< "$KEEP"
416	echo
417	echo "Kept frames: $CLEAN_DIR/, $OVERLAY_DIR/, $SCOOT_DIR/ (logs beside them). Full sequences: $EXT/."
418	echo "RESULT: all three captures checked; $kept frames kept."
419

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# sessions/a7/capture_strips.sh — A7 Step 7: the LAND and SCOOT fixture strips (CHANGE-BRIEF.md, "Evidence and frame
# strips"). Written by the agent (Step 7a session); Kiran reviews and runs it. Every frame it keeps is a FIXTURE
# frame from res://previews/*_preview.tscn, not gameplay evidence; landing-r0 stays the separate gameplay reference.
#
# Usage, from the repository root (needs a window; do not press keys in the Godot window while it records):
#   bash sessions/a7/capture_strips.sh [RUN]
# RUN is the revision name, default r0 (for example: bash sessions/a7/capture_strips.sh r1). It must be letters,
# digits, '.', '_' or '-' only. Below, <RUN> stands for it.
#
# 1. Refuses to start if captures/land/<RUN>, captures/scoot/<RUN> or any
#    ~/Documents/a7-reference/captures-full/{land-<RUN>-clean,land-<RUN>-overlay,scoot-<RUN>} directory already exists.
# 2. Runs windowed Movie Maker three times, each run's output teed to a log:
#      land  --fixed-fps 30                     -> captures/land/<RUN>/clean/    log captures/land/<RUN>/land_clean.log
#      land  --fixed-fps 30 --debug-collisions  -> captures/land/<RUN>/overlay/  log captures/land/<RUN>/land_overlay.log
#      scoot --fixed-fps 60                     -> captures/scoot/<RUN>/         log captures/scoot/<RUN>/scoot.log
#    Movie Maker writes frame<NNNNNNNN>.png, one per rendered frame counted from 0 (and frame.wav).
# 3. Checks every run before anything is moved: Godot exit 0, the preview's own result line with problems=0, no
#    SCRIPT ERROR / Failed loading resource, contiguous FRAME lines, contiguous PNG numbers from 0, and
#    PNG count == FRAME line count. PNG index = FRAME index - (index of the first FRAME line); the offset is printed.
#    Land: the TRIGGER frame's PNG exists, and frames trigger-1 .. trigger+4 show FALL, rig 0, 2, 4, 6 and IDLE at
#    tick 8 in the log. Scoot: one frame before, on and after every SWAP and WRAP line, with the expected cell and
#    clip frame. Every kept PNG must be 1280 x 720.
# 4. Only if every check passed: moves each run's full Movie Maker output (all frame* files) to
#    ~/Documents/a7-reference/captures-full/<run>/ (with a copy of its log), then copies the frames to read back into
#    the repository under names that carry the rig frame or clip frame, and prints a table of them.
# If anything fails it prints STOPPED and exits 1. A failure in step 3 moves nothing; the captures stay where
# Movie Maker wrote them.

set -Eeuo pipefail
trap 'rc=$?; echo "STOPPED: command \"$BASH_COMMAND\" failed with exit $rc (line $LINENO)" >&2' ERR

stop() {
	echo "STOPPED: $*" >&2
	exit 1
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- preflight (nothing is created before these pass)

REPO="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
if [ "$(pwd -P)" != "$(cd "$REPO" && pwd -P)" ]; then
	stop "run this from the repository root: $REPO"
fi
if [ "$#" -gt 1 ]; then
	stop "usage: bash sessions/a7/capture_strips.sh [RUN]  (one optional argument, default r0; got $#)"
fi
RUN="${1:-r0}"
if ! [[ "$RUN" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ ]]; then
	stop "run name '$RUN' must be letters, digits, '.', '_' or '-' only"
fi
echo "capture_strips.sh: run name $RUN"
LAND_DIR="captures/land/$RUN"
SCOOT_DIR="captures/scoot/$RUN"
CLEAN_DIR="$LAND_DIR/clean"
OVERLAY_DIR="$LAND_DIR/overlay"
CLEAN_LOG="$LAND_DIR/land_clean.log"
OVERLAY_LOG="$LAND_DIR/land_overlay.log"
SCOOT_LOG="$SCOOT_DIR/scoot.log"
EXT="$HOME/Documents/a7-reference/captures-full"
EXT_CLEAN="$EXT/land-$RUN-clean"
EXT_OVERLAY="$EXT/land-$RUN-overlay"
EXT_SCOOT="$EXT/scoot-$RUN"
WANT_SIZE="1280 x 720"

for d in "$LAND_DIR" "$SCOOT_DIR"; do
	if [ -e "$d" ]; then
		stop "$d already exists. Check what it is and move it yourself; this script never overwrites a capture."
	fi
done
for d in "$EXT_CLEAN" "$EXT_OVERLAY" "$EXT_SCOOT"; do
	if [ -e "$d" ]; then
		stop "$d already exists. Move it aside first; this script never overwrites a full sequence."
	fi
done
for tool in git godot timeout tee awk sed grep sort wc tr file mkdir mv cp; do
	if ! command -v "$tool" > /dev/null; then
		stop "required command not found: $tool"
	fi
done
for f in godot/previews/land_preview.tscn godot/previews/land_preview.gd godot/previews/scoot_preview.tscn godot/previews/scoot_preview.gd; do
	if [ ! -f "$f" ]; then
		stop "$f is missing"
	fi
done

echo "capture_strips.sh: HEAD $(git rev-parse HEAD), godot $(godot --version)"
echo "Do not press keys in the Godot window while it records: real key events reach the game."

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- helpers

strip_ansi() {   # file -> stdout without terminal colour codes
	LC_ALL=C sed -e $'s/\033\\[[0-9;]*m//g' "$1"
}

kv() {           # line key -> the value of key=value in the line, or nothing
	awk -v k="$2" '{ for (i = 1; i <= NF; i++) if (index($i, k "=") == 1) { print substr($i, length(k) + 2); exit } }' <<< "$1"
}

clip_frame() {   # clip time in seconds -> nearest 1/60 s timeline frame
	awk -v t="$1" 'BEGIN { printf "%d", t * 60 + 0.5 }'
}

near_frame() {   # clip time, frame: exit 0 if the time is that frame within 1e-3 frame
	awk -v t="$1" -v n="$2" 'BEGIN { d = t * 60 - n; if (d < 0) d = -d; exit (d < 0.001 ? 0 : 1) }'
}

run_capture() {  # label fps scene outdir log debug_collisions(0|1)
	local label="$1" fps="$2" scene="$3" outdir="$4" log="$5" debug="$6" rc=0 bad flags
	mkdir -p "$outdir"
	flags="--fixed-fps $fps"
	if [ "$debug" = "1" ]; then
		flags="$flags --debug-collisions"
	fi
	echo
	echo "=== $label: Movie Maker, $flags, $scene -> $outdir/"
	if [ "$debug" = "1" ]; then
		timeout 1800 godot --path godot --fixed-fps "$fps" --debug-collisions --write-movie "$REPO/$outdir/frame.png" "$scene" 2>&1 | tee "$log" || rc=$?
	else
		timeout 1800 godot --path godot --fixed-fps "$fps" --write-movie "$REPO/$outdir/frame.png" "$scene" 2>&1 | tee "$log" || rc=$?
	fi
	if [ "$rc" != "0" ]; then
		stop "$label: godot (or tee) exited $rc; see $log. Nothing was moved."
	fi
	bad="$( { strip_ansi "$log" | grep -cE 'SCRIPT ERROR|Failed loading resource'; } || true)"
	if [ "$bad" != "0" ]; then
		stop "$label: $bad SCRIPT ERROR / Failed loading resource lines in $log. Nothing was moved."
	fi
	echo "$label: godot exit 0"
}

FRAMES_TXT=""
F0=""
NFR=""
load_frames() {  # label log: FRAME lines into FRAMES_TXT; first index F0; count NFR; checks they are contiguous
	FRAMES_TXT="$( { strip_ansi "$2" | grep -E '^FRAME [0-9]+ '; } || true)"
	if [ -z "$FRAMES_TXT" ]; then
		stop "$1: no FRAME lines in $2"
	fi
	NFR="$(wc -l <<< "$FRAMES_TXT" | tr -d '[:space:]')"
	F0="$(awk 'NR == 1 { print $2 }' <<< "$FRAMES_TXT")"
	if ! awk 'NR == 1 { f0 = $2 } $2 != f0 + NR - 1 { bad = 1 } END { exit bad ? 1 : 0 }' <<< "$FRAMES_TXT"; then
		stop "$1: FRAME indices in $2 are not contiguous"
	fi
}

frame_line() {   # index -> the FRAME line with that process-frame index (from FRAMES_TXT)
	awk -v f="$1" '$1 == "FRAME" && $2 == f { print; exit }' <<< "$FRAMES_TXT"
}

NPNG=""
W=""
check_pngs() {   # label dir: counts frame<N>.png in NPNG, digit width in W; checks the numbers are 0..NPNG-1
	local names nums
	names="$( { ls "$2" | grep -E '^frame[0-9]+\.png$'; } || true)"
	if [ -z "$names" ]; then
		stop "$1: Movie Maker wrote no frame<N>.png in $2"
	fi
	NPNG="$(wc -l <<< "$names" | tr -d '[:space:]')"
	W="$(awk 'NR == 1 { print length($0) - 9 }' <<< "$names")"
	if ! awk -v w="$W" 'length($0) - 9 != w { bad = 1 } END { exit bad ? 1 : 0 }' <<< "$names"; then
		stop "$1: PNG names in $2 do not all have $W digits"
	fi
	nums="$(sed -E 's/^frame0*([0-9]+)\.png$/\1/' <<< "$names" | sort -n)"
	if ! awk '$1 != NR - 1 { bad = 1 } END { exit bad ? 1 : 0 }' <<< "$nums"; then
		stop "$1: PNG numbers in $2 are not contiguous from 0"
	fi
}

png_name() {     # index -> frame<index, W digits>.png
	printf "frame%0${W}d.png" "$1"
}

check_size() {   # label png
	local size
	size="$( { file -b "$2" | grep -oE '[0-9]+ x [0-9]+' | head -n 1; } || true)"
	if [ "$size" != "$WANT_SIZE" ]; then
		stop "$1: $2 is '${size:-unknown}', expected $WANT_SIZE. Nothing was moved."
	fi
}

map_run() {      # label outdir log: loads FRAME lines and PNGs, checks the counts match, prints the offset
	load_frames "$1" "$3"
	check_pngs "$1" "$2"
	if [ "$NPNG" != "$NFR" ]; then
		stop "$1: Movie Maker wrote $NPNG PNGs but $3 has $NFR FRAME lines, so PNGs cannot be matched to log frames. Nothing was moved."
	fi
	echo "$1: $NPNG PNGs = $NFR FRAME lines; first FRAME line is process frame $F0, so PNG index = FRAME index - $F0 (offset $F0)"
}

KEEP=""          # one line per kept frame: outdir \t ext \t source png \t new name \t frame \t png \t tick \t pose \t clip \t t \t cell \t expect
keep() {
	KEEP="$KEEP$(printf '%s\t' "$@")"$'\n'
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- land: trigger - 1 .. trigger + 4

CLEAN_TRIGGER=""
OVERLAY_TRIGGER=""
select_land() {  # variant(clean|overlay) outdir log ext
	local variant="$1" outdir="$2" log="$3" ext="$4" label="land $1"
	local result trig n tf td aligned tp rel fr line pose clip t tick cell rel_tick rig tag expect png ok
	map_run "$label" "$outdir" "$log"
	result="$( { strip_ansi "$log" | grep -E '^LAND PREVIEW: .* problems=0$'; } || true)"
	if [ -z "$result" ]; then
		stop "$label: no 'LAND PREVIEW: ... problems=0' line in $log (see its PROBLEM lines)"
	fi
	trig="$( { strip_ansi "$log" | grep -E '^TRIGGER '; } || true)"
	n=0
	if [ -n "$trig" ]; then
		n="$(wc -l <<< "$trig" | tr -d '[:space:]')"
	fi
	if [ "$n" != "1" ]; then
		stop "$label: expected exactly one TRIGGER line in $log, found $n"
	fi
	tf="$(kv "$trig" frame)"
	td="$(kv "$trig" touchdown_tick)"
	aligned="$(kv "$trig" aligned)"
	if [ "$aligned" != "true" ]; then
		stop "$label: TRIGGER line says aligned=$aligned: $trig"
	fi
	tp=$((tf - F0))
	if [ ! -f "$outdir/$(png_name "$tp")" ]; then
		stop "$label: TRIGGER frame $tf -> PNG index $tp, but $outdir/$(png_name "$tp") does not exist"
	fi
	echo "$label: TRIGGER frame=$tf (touchdown tick $td) -> PNG index $tp = $(png_name "$tp")"
	if [ "$variant" = "clean" ]; then
		CLEAN_TRIGGER="$tf/$tp"
	else
		OVERLAY_TRIGGER="$tf/$tp"
	fi
	for rel in -1 0 1 2 3 4; do
		fr=$((tf + rel))
		png=$((fr - F0))
		line="$(frame_line "$fr")"
		if [ -z "$line" ]; then
			stop "$label: no FRAME line for trigger $rel (frame $fr)"
		fi
		pose="$(kv "$line" pose)"
		clip="$(kv "$line" clip)"
		t="$(kv "$line" t)"
		tick="$(kv "$line" tick)"
		cell="$(kv "$line" cell)"
		rel_tick=$((tick - td))
		ok=1
		case "$rel" in
			-1)
				[ "$pose" = "FALL" ] && [ "$clip" = "-" ] || ok=0
				tag="trig-1_FALL"
				expect="Airborne FALL before contact"
				;;
			4)
				[ "$pose" = "IDLE" ] && [ "$clip" = "-" ] && [ "$rel_tick" = "8" ] || ok=0
				tag="trig+4_tick8_IDLE-handoff"
				expect="Tick 8: IDLE hand-off without a pop, seam or anchor shift"
				;;
			*)
				rig=$((2 * rel))
				if [ "$pose" != "LAND" ] || [ "$clip" != "land" ] || [ "$rel_tick" != "$rig" ] || ! near_frame "$t" "$rig"; then
					ok=0
				fi
				case "$rel" in
					0) tag="trig+0_rig0_impact"; expect="Frame 0: partial squash and planted feet" ;;
					1) tag="trig+1_rig2_deepest-squash"; expect="Frame 2: deepest squash, about the height of the low box" ;;
					2) tag="trig+2_rig4_same-squash"; expect="Frame 4: same squash, now beginning recovery" ;;
					3) tag="trig+3_rig6_eased-rise"; expect="Frame 6: eased rise, joined cut and fixed feet" ;;
				esac
				;;
		esac
		if [ "$ok" != "1" ]; then
			stop "$label: trigger $rel (frame $fr) does not show what the strip needs ($tag): $line"
		fi
		check_size "$label" "$outdir/$(png_name "$png")"
		keep "$outdir" "$ext" "$(png_name "$png")" "land_${variant}_${tag}_png$(printf "%0${W}d" "$png").png" \
			"$fr" "$png" "$tick" "$pose" "$clip" "$t" "$cell" "$expect"
	done
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- scoot: one before, on and one after every swap and wrap

select_scoot() { # outdir log ext
	local outdir="$1" log="$2" ext="$3" label="scoot"
	local result events n ev kind kind_lc f dir k pos off fr png line pose clip t tick cell cf want_cell want_cf expect
	local right_swap=0 right_wrap=0 left_swap=0 left_wrap=0
	map_run "$label" "$outdir" "$log"
	result="$( { strip_ansi "$log" | grep -E '^SCOOT PREVIEW: .* problems=0$'; } || true)"
	if [ -z "$result" ]; then
		stop "$label: no 'SCOOT PREVIEW: ... problems=0' line in $log (see its PROBLEM lines)"
	fi
	events="$( { strip_ansi "$log" | grep -E '^(SWAP|WRAP) '; } || true)"
	if [ -z "$events" ]; then
		stop "$label: no SWAP or WRAP lines in $log"
	fi
	n="$(wc -l <<< "$events" | tr -d '[:space:]')"
	echo "$label: $n SWAP/WRAP lines"
	while IFS= read -r ev; do
		kind="$(awk '{ print $1 }' <<< "$ev")"
		kind_lc="$(tr 'A-Z' 'a-z' <<< "$kind")"
		f="$(kv "$ev" frame)"
		dir="$(kv "$ev" dir)"
		case "$dir/$kind" in
			right/SWAP) right_swap=$((right_swap + 1)); k=$right_swap ;;
			right/WRAP) right_wrap=$((right_wrap + 1)); k=$right_wrap ;;
			left/SWAP) left_swap=$((left_swap + 1)); k=$left_swap ;;
			left/WRAP) left_wrap=$((left_wrap + 1)); k=$left_wrap ;;
			*) stop "$label: unexpected event line: $ev" ;;
		esac
		for pos in before on after; do
			case "$pos" in
				before) off=-1 ;;
				on) off=0 ;;
				after) off=1 ;;
			esac
			fr=$((f + off))
			png=$((fr - F0))
			line="$(frame_line "$fr")"
			if [ -z "$line" ]; then
				stop "$label: no FRAME line $pos $kind at frame $f"
			fi
			pose="$(kv "$line" pose)"
			clip="$(kv "$line" clip)"
			t="$(kv "$line" t)"
			tick="$(kv "$line" tick)"
			cell="$(kv "$line" cell)"
			if [ "$clip" != "scoot" ]; then
				stop "$label: frame $fr ($pos $kind at $f) is not in the scoot clip: $line"
			fi
			cf="$(clip_frame "$t")"
			case "$kind/$pos" in
				SWAP/before) want_cell=0; want_cf=6; expect="Cell 0 (A), last tick of the A hold" ;;
				SWAP/on) want_cell=1; want_cf=7; expect="Cell 1 (B) at the swap: feet registered, no jump" ;;
				SWAP/after) want_cell=1; want_cf=8; expect="Cell 1 (B), second tick of the B hold" ;;
				WRAP/before) want_cell=1; want_cf=13; expect="Cell 1 (B), last frame of the loop" ;;
				WRAP/on) want_cell=0; want_cf=0; expect="Cell 0 (A) at the wrap: no hesitation, feet registered" ;;
				WRAP/after) want_cell=0; want_cf=1; expect="Cell 0 (A), second tick of the A hold" ;;
			esac
			if [ "$cell" != "$want_cell" ] || [ "$cf" != "$want_cf" ] || ! near_frame "$t" "$want_cf"; then
				stop "$label: frame $fr ($pos $kind at $f) shows cell $cell at clip frame $cf, expected cell $want_cell at $want_cf: $line"
			fi
			check_size "$label" "$outdir/$(png_name "$png")"
			keep "$outdir" "$ext" "$(png_name "$png")" \
				"scoot_${dir}_${kind_lc}${k}_${pos}_clip${cf}_cell${cell}_png$(printf "%0${W}d" "$png").png" \
				"$fr" "$png" "$tick" "$pose" "$clip" "$t" "$cell" "$expect, facing $dir"
		done
	done <<< "$events"
	echo "$label: right $right_swap swaps, $right_wrap wraps; left $left_swap swaps, $left_wrap wraps"
	if [ "$right_swap" -lt 2 ] || [ "$right_wrap" -lt 2 ] || [ "$left_swap" -lt 2 ] || [ "$left_wrap" -lt 2 ]; then
		stop "$label: expected at least two swaps and two wraps in each direction"
	fi
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- move the full sequences out, copy the kept frames back

move_full() {    # outdir ext log
	local outdir="$1" ext="$2" log="$3" f left
	mkdir -p "$ext"
	for f in "$outdir"/frame*; do
		if [ ! -e "$f" ]; then
			stop "no Movie Maker files to move in $outdir"
		fi
		mv -n "$f" "$ext/"
	done
	left="$( { ls "$outdir" | grep -cE '^frame'; } || true)"
	if [ "$left" != "0" ]; then
		stop "$left Movie Maker files are still in $outdir after the move"
	fi
	cp "$log" "$ext/"
	echo "moved the full sequence: $outdir/frame* -> $ext/ (with a copy of $(basename "$log"))"
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- run

run_capture "land clean" 30 res://previews/land_preview.tscn "$CLEAN_DIR" "$CLEAN_LOG" 0
run_capture "land overlay" 30 res://previews/land_preview.tscn "$OVERLAY_DIR" "$OVERLAY_LOG" 1
run_capture "scoot" 60 res://previews/scoot_preview.tscn "$SCOOT_DIR" "$SCOOT_LOG" 0

echo
echo "=== checks (nothing is moved unless all pass)"
select_land clean "$CLEAN_DIR" "$CLEAN_LOG" "$EXT_CLEAN"
select_land overlay "$OVERLAY_DIR" "$OVERLAY_LOG" "$EXT_OVERLAY"
if [ "$CLEAN_TRIGGER" = "$OVERLAY_TRIGGER" ]; then
	echo "land: clean and overlay TRIGGER frame/PNG are the same: $CLEAN_TRIGGER"
else
	echo "land: NOTE clean TRIGGER frame/PNG $CLEAN_TRIGGER differs from overlay $OVERLAY_TRIGGER (each run checked on its own)"
fi
select_scoot "$SCOOT_DIR" "$SCOOT_LOG" "$EXT_SCOOT"

echo
echo "=== moving"
move_full "$CLEAN_DIR" "$EXT_CLEAN" "$CLEAN_LOG"
move_full "$OVERLAY_DIR" "$EXT_OVERLAY" "$OVERLAY_LOG"
move_full "$SCOOT_DIR" "$EXT_SCOOT" "$SCOOT_LOG"
kept=0
while IFS=$'\t' read -r outdir ext src name _rest; do
	if [ -z "$outdir" ]; then
		continue
	fi
	if [ ! -f "$ext/$src" ]; then
		stop "$ext/$src missing after the move"
	fi
	if [ -e "$outdir/$name" ]; then
		stop "$outdir/$name already exists (a frame kept twice?)"
	fi

# CHAR-SCOOT-SHEET.png: credits and provenance

- **File:** `godot/assets/art/CHAR-SCOOT-SHEET.png`, 2048 × 1024 RGBA, SHA-256 `30b0ab635693477205cb9611160dcafd735a1f3e67ba7ffdb4fc3556eee04736`.
- **What it is:** a two-cell sprite sheet for the A7 `scoot` clip. Cell 0 (x 0–1023) is `CHAR-SCOOT-A.png` and cell 1 (x 1024–2047) is `CHAR-SCOOT-B.png`, packed side by side with no cropping, resizing or padding. The packing tool `godot/tools/make_scoot_sheet.gd` was written by Claude Code (`sessions/a7/session-3a.jsonl`) and reviewed and run by Kiran Gowda on 2026-11-16. Its checks found 0 mismatched pixels in each cell against its source, in memory and after reloading from disk (`logs/make_scoot_sheet_run1.log`); a re-run left the sheet unchanged (`logs/make_scoot_sheet_run2.log`).
- **Sources:** `godot/assets/art/CHAR-SCOOT-A.png` (SHA-256 `6aa35cf27aa3ed6202f2d0254f1defe456d0db4a387981cf0104be03af6b916a`) and `godot/assets/art/CHAR-SCOOT-B.png` (SHA-256 `f95dacdb13614d9ed7d4a5798e3bf6df8902d5dcd5186f368631bcce0a4bb271`), unchanged since commit `e6f1644`, with identical copies in `art/game/`.
- **Author:** Kiran Gowda. Generated locally with Stable Diffusion XL Base 1.0 (Stability AI) in Draw Things 26.0924.0, image to image from pose guides built from CHAR-REF, then cleaned and cut out. The full record is in `ASSET-LOG.md` (prompt at lines 10–11, CHAR-SCOOT-B at 57–85, CHAR-SCOOT-A at 112–121, cut-out at 166). The model and tools are in `SOURCES.md`.
- **Terms:** [CreativeML Open RAIL++-M](https://huggingface.co/stabilityai/stable-diffusion-xl-base-1.0/blob/main/LICENSE.md), dated 2023-07-26, checked 2026-11-16. The public repository and the film contain this artwork, not the model weights. The prompt names no living artist, brand or copyrighted character.
- **Import settings:** `CHAR-SCOOT-SHEET.png.import` has the same `[params]` as `CHAR-SCOOT-A.png.import`. Godot's first import set `mipmaps/generate=false` (`logs/import_after_sheet.log`); Kiran changed it to `true` and re-imported (`logs/import_after_sheet_mipmaps.log`).

## A7 — landing, r1: Claude's comparison (agent)

Written by the agent (Claude Code, documentation session `sessions/a7/session-8.jsonl`) on 2026-11-17. **Kiran's r1 verdict above was written first, before this comparison, and is his own reading. This entry is not his verdict.** It compares the r1 frames with my r1 prediction (above) and with r0.

Frames read, full size only (1280 × 720, unzoomed; this session had no shell, so no crop, zoom, byte comparison or checksum): the six clean frames of each run, `captures/land/r0/clean/` (process frames 104–109) and `captures/land/r1/clean/` (145–150), and one r1 overlay frame, `captures/land/r1/overlay/land_overlay_trig+1_rig2_deepest-squash_png00000147.png`. As in my r0 reading, every size is my estimate from the full frame, about ±2 px, not a measurement.

Logs: `captures/land/r1/land_clean.log` and `land_overlay.log` both report `TRIGGER frame=146 touchdown_tick=293 ... aligned=true`, `STRIP rel_ticks=[0, 2, 4, 6, 8] layout_30fps=true`, every `STRIP` line `ok=true`, and `LAND PREVIEW: trigger_frame=146 touchdown_tick=293 problems=0`. So r1 shows the same rig frames as r0 (0, 2, 4, 6, then IDLE at tick 8). The r1 clean run's trigger is frame 146, while the r0 clean run's was frame 105 (touchdown tick 211). In the r0 clean log the player's `ptick` starts counting at frame 79; in the r1 logs it starts at frame 120. I did not look into why. The strip positions relative to the trigger are the same.

| Kept frame (r0 → r1) | My prediction | What I see in r1 next to r0 | Matched? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| trigger − 1, FALL (104 → 145) | Same as r0; the clip is not playing | The same FALL drawing (dot eyes, flat mouth), about the same height above the plate rim. | Matched, as far as an unzoomed still shows |
| rig 0, impact (105 → 146) | Same as r0; frame-0 key unchanged | To my eye the jelly is the same: same top, width and bottom edge on the rim. (Background difference: in r0 there is a dark smudge on the third plate that is absent in r1 146; it is not on the jelly.) | Matched |
| rig 2, deepest squash (106 → 147) | About 1 game px flatter (≈ 43 px, r0 ≈ 44), same width, feet in the same place | Same width and the same bottom edge on the rim. The top edge looks at most about 1 px lower than in r0. That is inside my ±2 px estimate error, so I cannot confirm the 1.007 px difference from these stills. I see nothing that contradicts it. | Not contradicted; not confirmable at this resolution |
| rig 4, same squash (107 → 148) | Identical to r1's rig 2 | The jelly looks the same as in r1 147. The visible differences between the two are only in the crumbs. As at rig 2, any change from r0 is at most about 1 px. | Matched on "same as rig 2"; the r0 difference is not confirmable, as at rig 2 |
| rig 6, eased rise (108 → 149) | About 0.25 px lower than r0; not expected to be visible | I see no difference from r0 in the jelly. | Matched (no visible change, as predicted) |
| tick 8, IDLE hand-off (109 → 150) | Same as r0 (original IDLE sprite) | The original IDLE sprite, bottom edge in the same place on the plate as r0. | Matched |

# TUNING — Assignment 6

Every revision records Claude's prediction, the strips before and after, Claude's comparison and my verdict in the running game (CHANGE-BRIEF.md; assignment Step 4). Strips are **fixture captures** of the preview scenes in `godot/previews/`, rendered by Movie Maker at 30 fps (`--fixed-fps 30`) with fixed seeds on the preview instances only. Files are numbered from 0, so strip frame N is `frameNNNNNNNN.png`.

## Effect A — Landing crumb puff

### 2026-11-07 — Effect A, r0: my first verdict, before Claude read anything
Strip: `captures/land_puff/r0/` (fixture capture; `land_puff_preview.tscn` with `retrigger` off; seeds 1001 and 1002; frames 10, 12, 15, 20, 30, 50). Effect settings: CHANGE-BRIEF.md Version 1, as built in commit `2bb6ebc`.
Where I looked: the running preview at the project's window size (1280 × 720), several runs, and the six strip frames.

What I saw (my words): In the live preview, I saw a quick puff that looked like white smoke under both jellies. At frame 12, it was easy to see on both the pale plate and the dark table. At frame 15, most of the crumbs were still under the jellies, so I didn't see the wide sideways fan I expected. The crumbs were gone by frame 20 and stayed gone in frames 30 and 50.

Claude's reading of r0: not yet requested.

### 2026-11-07 — Effect A, revision r1
What I saw (preview fixture and running game, 1280 × 720): my r0 verdict above. At frame 15 most crumbs were still under the jellies, with no wide sideways fan. In the running game a puff appeared at the jelly's feet on every landing, and the puffs all looked the same to me. On my r0 plate-edge attempt in the running game, I didn't see the two puffs overlap. That helped motivate trying a more visible sideways spread. I haven't verified overlap in r1.

Claude's reading of r0 (`sessions/a6/session-4a-reading.md`): frames 10, 30 and 50 match the intent; frame 12 does not have crumbs "out from behind both sides"; frame 15 fails, with a few crumbs just outside one edge and nothing near a jelly width out; frame 20 is empty. Its explanation: the LAND sprite is about 78 px wide, wider than the 52 px collision box the brief was sized to, and the push is too weak to carry crumbs past the visible edge. It read the frames unzoomed, because its three image-crop commands were denied.

Change: `radial_accel_curve` (`CurveTexture`) `(0, 1), (0.2, 0)` → `(0, 1), (0.18, 1), (0.2, 0)`, linear, approved by me. `radial_accel_min` / `radial_accel_max` unchanged at 4000 / 6500. Claude first proposed doubling the radial range to 8000 / 13000; I chose its curve-only alternative instead (`sessions/a6/prompt-4b.txt`). The agent made the edit and updated the configuration test's expected curve points (`sessions/a6/session-4c-reply.md`). My config run: 51 checks / 0 failures, exit 0.

Claude's prediction for r1 (`sessions/a6/session-4b-prediction.md`): frame 10 unchanged; frame 12 crumbs still mostly behind the jelly, no crumb centre clearing the visible edge, so still short of the brief; frame 15 about 60–75 % of crumbs clear the edge, mostly by 5–35 px, at most about 40 px, low, short of one jelly width; frame 20 empty or a few faint specks; frames 30 and 50 empty. Risk named: about one stray crumb per puff kicked upward. A cross-check simulation by Claude in chat (not Claude Code) used the same timing assumption and also predicted almost nothing past the edge at frame 12.

Claude's comparison of r1 with its prediction (`sessions/a6/session-4d-comparison.md`): frames 10, 20, 30 and 50 match. Frame 12 does **not** match: crumbs show about 5–15 px past both edges of both jellies, about 10 px further than predicted. Frame 15 partly matches: low fans on both sides of both jellies, near crumbs and height as predicted, but the farthest reach about 36–49 px beyond the visible edges, about 10 px beyond its predicted maximum; no stray high crumb seen. Its explanation: its model was one frame off, because the preview starts emission in `_process()` on frame 10 and frame 10 already shows crumbs, so frame 10 + n shows crumbs (n + 1)/30 s old. Inferred from the frames, not checked in Godot's source. Against the brief: frame 12 roughly meets "out from behind both sides"; frame 15 reaches about 0.7–0.95 of a jelly width beyond the edge, a little short of "about one jelly width".

My verdict (running game, 1280 × 720): **kept**, because the puff was easy to see when the jelly landed in the running game. In the frame comparison, r1 was already wider at frame 12 and spread farther past both sides by frame 15.

Strips: `captures/land_puff/r0/`, `captures/land_puff/r1/` (fixture captures, seeds 1001 and 1002, same preview).
Commits: the curve change (agent, approved by me), then strip r1, then this verdict with the brief revision, in that order.

## Effect B — Dome sugar glints

### 2026-11-07 — Effect B, r0: my first verdict, before Claude read anything
Strip: `captures/dome_glints/r0/` (fixture capture; `dome_glints_preview.tscn`; seed 2001 on the preview instance only; `restart()` at frame 10, `emitting = false` at frame 70; Movie Maker at 30 fps, 150 frames; strip frames 10, 12, 40, 70, 85, 145). Effect settings: CHANGE-BRIEF.md Version 1, as built in commit `f2e5b26`.
Where I looked: the running preview at the project's window size (1280 × 720) and the r0 capture.

What I saw (my words): I ran the live preview and checked the Effect B r0 capture myself. The glints were already visible around the dome at frame 10, and I saw more of them there than at frame 40. I didn't notice them thinning out by frame 85. By frame 145, no glints were visible.

Claude's reading of r0: not yet requested.

### 2026-11-07 — Effect B, revision r1
What I saw (preview fixture and running game, 1280 × 720): my r0 verdict above. The glints were already visible at frame 10, with more there than at frame 40, and no thinning by frame 85. In the running game they were visible when the dome first appeared in the intro, faded gradually after I won, and were easy to see against both the dark wall and the glass.

Claude's reading of r0 (`sessions/a6/session-7a-reading.md`): frames 10, 12, 70 and 145 match the intent; 40 and 85 miss it. It counted about 14 visible dots at frame 10 and about 9 at 40, mostly over the glass, and no thinning from 70 to 85. Its explanation: alpha and size both climb over the first 0.2 of life (about 0.48 s), so the glints missing after the stop are the ones still fading in, and the brief's "fades in over about 0.5 s" contradicts its frame-85 "fewer near the glass". It also inferred, untested, that `lifetime_randomness = 0.3` only shortens lives (1.68–2.4 s), so fewer than 24 are alive on average. It read the frames unzoomed, because its two image-crop commands were denied.

Change: `color_ramp` (`Gradient_life`) offsets `(0, 0.2, 0.75, 1)` → `(0, 0.08, 0.75, 1)`, colours unchanged, approved by me. `scale_curve` unchanged. The agent made the edit and updated the configuration test's `RAMP_OFFSETS` (`sessions/a6/session-7b-reply.md`). My config run: 45 checks / 0 failures, exit 0.

Claude's prediction for r1 (`sessions/a6/session-7a-reading.md`): same positions as r0; frame 10 a few more small bright dots low in the glass, about 16 to 18 visible; frame 40 about 12 to 14, still well under 24 and mostly over the glass; frame 70 full; frame 85 the lower glass visibly emptier than at 70, 3 to 5 fewer dots; frame 145 empty.

My byte comparison (Terminal, `cmp` on each r0/r1 strip-frame pair): frames 10, 12, 40, 70 and 85 differ between r0 and r1, and frame 145 is identical, so the change took effect in the render.

Claude's comparison of r1 with its prediction (`sessions/a6/session-7c-comparison.md`): its `shasum` command was denied, so it compared file sizes instead. Its visual review found the same positions and motion as r0, but no extra visible dots at 10 or 40 (about 9 at 40), and no clearer thinning from 70 to 85 than in r0 (the file shrinks by 543 bytes in r1 and 539 in r0). Its explanation: young glints are still tiny while `scale_curve` grows them, so size, not alpha, limits how visible they are; it called its count prediction its own mistake.

My own look at the strips: the two frame-40 images looked nearly identical. A pair of screenshots looked slightly less crowded inside the glass at frame 85 than at frame 70, but Preview didn't show which capture folder that pair came from, so I don't count it as a confirmed r1 result.

Where Claude and I disagree: at full frame size Claude saw no visible difference between r0 and r1, while in the running game I found the glints noticeably easier to see in the intro. My verdict in the running game decides.

My verdict (running game, 1280 × 720): **kept**. I watched the intro in the running game, and the glints were noticeably easier to see. I couldn't tell whether they were brighter or whether more were visible. The frame comparison didn't show clearer thinning from frame 70 to 85, so I'm keeping r1 for how it looks in the intro.

# TEST-REPORT — Jelly Hop: Fork From Above

- **Source revision tested:** `23ae39c` (`23ae39ce6c84b683670640d6ef51502376896dbe`, on GitHub `kirangowda3101/walker-jellyhop-kiran-g`, branch `main`).
- **Changes since then:** this report and its evidence are committed after it, together with one fix to a check script (`tools/check_game_audio.py`, see §1). No game code or asset changed after `23ae39c`.
- **Engine:** Godot `4.7.2.stable.official.ed1daf0bf` (GL Compatibility renderer).
- **Machine:** macOS 26.5.1 (build 25F80), MacBook Pro, Apple M4, 16 GB, arm64.
- **Playtester:** Kiran only. There are no other playtesters.
- **Human playtest vs automated runs:** the human playtest is Kiran's (§4–§7, quoted word for word). Everything marked "automated" or "scripted" drives the game with scripted input or fixtures; none of it is a human playtest.
- **Date:** 2026-10-03.

## 1. Startup and controls (from a fresh copy)

Verified from a fresh clone of GitHub into a temporary folder outside the working repository. Full log: `evidence/test-fresh-copy.txt`, with the complete outputs in `evidence/test-fresh-*-full.txt`.

```
git clone https://github.com/kirangowda3101/walker-jellyhop-kiran-g.git <tmp>/fresh-clone      # exit 0; HEAD 23ae39c
cd <tmp>/fresh-clone
/Applications/Godot.app/Contents/MacOS/Godot --headless --path godot --import                   # exit 0
bash tools/run_slice_checks.sh                                                                 # see below
./walker-jumpman.command                                                                       # the game launches; closed after 8 s, no errors logged
```

- **The fresh copy has no `.godot` import cache.** That's expected (it is git-ignored); the import builds it.
- **First check run at `23ae39c`: STOPPED at the game audio checks.** 7 of 8 checks failed only on "process-log SHA match False"; every audio measurement passed (start 0 ms, peaks, loudness, loop on).
  - **Cause:** `tools/check_game_audio.py` looked up each file's processing record by the *absolute path* of the original working copy, which doesn't exist in a clone at another path.
  - **Fix (committed with this report):** look the record up by the repo-relative path `audio/game/<ID>.ogg`.
  - **Second run in the fresh copy,** with the fixed script copied in: `ALL SLICE CHECKS PASSED`:
    - art 18/18 and audio 7/7 copies byte-identical
    - game audio 8/0
    - mechanics 25/0
    - keyboard 12/0
    - slice 61/0
    - 7 screenshots at 1280 × 720
    - an 8 s launch with no errors
  - **Not a game bug,** but a real portability bug in a check; `23ae39c` as committed fails this check from a fresh copy.
- **Every asset the game loads is present** (tracked in git):
  - 18 PNG in `godot/assets/art/`: the 12 poses `CHAR-<POSE>.png` and the 6 environment images `ENV-ROOM/TABLE/PLATE/SAUCE/FORK/DOME`;
  - 7 OGG in `godot/assets/audio/`: the 6 sound effects and `MUS-LOOP`, with `MUS-LOOP.ogg.import` set to `loop=true`.
  - The art and audio copies are byte-identical to `art/game/` and `audio/game/`.
  - The largest tracked file is 0.85 MB; there are no MP3 or MP4 files.
- **Requirements for running the checks:** the Godot app at `/Applications/Godot.app`. The game-audio check also needs the Python environment `~/Documents/jellyhop-audio-env` (it is outside the repository). Playing the game needs only Godot.
- **Controls** (SLICE-BRIEF §6), checked by `godot/tests/test_keyboard.gd` with synthetic key events (12/0):

|---|---|---|
| Move | ← / → or A / D | `keyboard-move-d`, `-a`, `-right-arrow`, `-left-arrow` |
| Hop | Space, ↑ or W | `keyboard-jump-space`, `-up`, `-w` |
| Pause / resume | Esc | `escape-pause`, `escape-resume` |
| Skip intro / play again | any key (never hops or moves) | `any-key-start`, `any-key-replay`; slice `skip-key-no-hop-no-move-*`, `restart-key-no-hop-first-plate-reset` |

Kiran played the game from the Godot editor (F5) in the slice setup review (FRICTIONAL.md, 2026-10-03 slice entry), and played it again for the three Batch 3 auditions and this playtest.

## 2. Character against the sheet

`evidence/test-character-vs-sheet.png` puts each CHARACTER-SHEET pose (`design/character/poses.svg`, cropped from the sheet) beside the in-engine pose facing right and facing left.
- The in-engine screenshots are rendered by the game and captured by `godot/tests/capture_poses.gd`, at 4× zoom on plate 1. The active collision box is outlined in magenta by the capture script only.
- Single captures: `evidence/test-poses/<POSE>-R|L.png`; boxes: `evidence/test-poses/boxes.txt`. The image was built by `tools/test_report_images.py`.

- **Facing:** every pose flips for left (`flip_h` true facing left, false facing right). The jelly keeps facing the way it last moved (automated: `pose-flip-keeps-facing`).
- **Size and anchor (automated):** the resting cube is 64.2 × 63.8 px on screen (`pose-idle-size-64`), and the art's bottom is flush with the box bottom within 0.11 px (`pose-bottom-flush`).

- **Mismatches with the collision rules:**
  1. **Crouch (ANTIC) keeps the standing box** (52 × 58). The sheet gives the crouch the low box (52 × 44). In this build the crouch is a visual-only pose shown for the first 4 ticks after takeoff. With the low box in the air, the starter's low-ceiling check failed: the feet rose 48 px under a 40 px ceiling gap. So the code keeps the standing box, and the check was not changed. In the comparison the box reaches above the squashed art.
  2. **Splat and re-forming:** the sheet says "hits off". In the engine the collider stays the standing box (it keeps the body on the plate), and hits are off because hazards are not checked in the SPLAT and REFORM states (automated: `duplicate-death-ignored`, `twenty-retries`). The magenta box drawn over the flat splat is that collider, not a hit zone.
  3. **Scoot A:** the standing box sits about 2 px above the art, the sheet's own watch item (failure #14). It has not been playtested separately near strikes.

### The process shader (Step 6)

I copied LandPuff's `ParticleProcessMaterial` into a scratch scene, made the copy unique, and converted it to a `ShaderMaterial` in the Godot 4.7.2 editor. I saved the generated shader unchanged as `godot/shaders/particles_generated.gdshader` and closed the scratch scene without saving it. The shader is 411 lines and is not used by the game. My Git status check showed only the new shader and its `.uid`.

| Item | Line(s) | What the code does |
|---|---|---|
| Shader type | 3 | `shader_type particles;` declares this as a particle shader. |
| `start()` | 257 | Sets up a particle when it starts or restarts. |
| `process()` | 309 | Updates the particle during simulation. |
| Initial velocity | 145, 296 | Line 145 picks a speed between the minimum and maximum using a seeded random value. Line 296 multiplies that speed by a direction picked within the spread and stores the result in `USERDATA1.xyz`. |
| Gravity | 343, 356, 372, 376 | Line 343 starts the force with gravity. Line 356 adds `force * DELTA` to the stored velocity. Line 372 combines that velocity with `controlled_displacement`, and line 376 assigns the result to `VELOCITY`. |
| Colour over life | 167, 384 | Line 167 samples the colour ramp using the particle’s age and multiplies the particle colour by the sample. Line 384 writes the resulting colour to `COLOR`. |
| Scale over life | 166, 396–398, 401–403 | Line 166 samples the scale curve using the particle’s age and multiplies the particle’s scale by the sample. Lines 396–398 apply it to the transform on the first frame, preserving each axis’s sign. Lines 401–403 apply the scale magnitude on later frames. |
| Setting tied to my brief | 254 | The shader samples the radial acceleration curve at the particle’s lifetime percentage and uses it to scale radial acceleration. My Effect A Revision 1 curve points are `(0, 1)`, `(0.18, 1)`, and `(0.2, 0)`. |

**Settings split.** Initial velocity, spread, gravity, radial acceleration, damping, and the colour and scale curves are used by the process shader. The particle's visible texture and blend mode belong to drawing. `z_index` controls draw order, and `visibility_rect` sets visibility bounds on the node. Amount, lifetime, one-shot, and explosiveness are emitter settings. The shader uses lifetime information during simulation, but the emitter configures the lifetime.
